answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a locked collateral bond plus a web of endorsements: an agent stakes real value and gets vouched by trusted peers before voting or earning. Reputation grows like a cedar, slow and rooted, so fake identities sink to the nadir of the ranking because nobody vouches for them. A thousand votes require a thousand separate bonds and a thousand distinct endorsers; since each may vouch only a few times, the cost climbs superlinearly. The vine of trust spreads only along verified links, making mass impersonation dearer than any payoff.
